tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
Most of this is already built. It landed in the last merge (`cb8e9fd9`, "in-app service keys"). Here's what exists, what can't leave `.env`, and what I'd still change.

## Already in the app

| Key | Where you enter it now | `.env` still needed? |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI API key | Settings → AI access | No (the `.env` value is only a fallback) |
| ChatGPT sign-in | Settings → AI access | No |
| OpenRouter API key | Settings → AI access | No (fallback only) |
| Enable Banking App ID and private key | Import → Connected banks, and Settings → Connected banks | No (fallback only) |
| Scalable Capital | Connect button with Scalable's login, no keys | No |
| AI models for each agent | Settings → AI and your data | No |

Keys are checked with the provider before they're saved. They're stored encrypted in the database and shown only by their last 4 characters, and you can replace or remove them in the app.

## What has to stay in `.env`

The rest of `.env` is the app's startup config. The app needs it before it can even connect to the database, so it can't be stored in the database:

- **`POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_*`**: how the app reaches and signs in to its own database.
- **`MONEO_OWNER_EMAIL` / `PASSWORD`**: the automatic owner sign-in.
- **`BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`**: the key that encrypts all the saved keys. If it were stored in the database next to them, the encryption would protect nothing.
- **`CRON_SECRET`**: protects the background job routes.

A new user never types any of these. `npm run setup` generates them all. So the file has to exist on disk, but nobody needs to open it. Moving it to another file such as `.data/config.json` would only rename it, so I'd keep `.env` and stop presenting it as something to fill in.

## Gaps for a new user (README and setup)

1. **No "what next" after setup.** The README's Run section ends at "open localhost:3000" and never says "now go to Settings → AI access and add a key or sign in with ChatGPT". I'd add a short **First run** checklist: AI (required for chat) → bank (optional) → Scalable (optional).
2. **`.env.example` still lists `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `ENABLE_BANKING_*` near the top.** A newcomer will think they need to fill them in. I'd move them to a clearly marked "legacy overrides, leave empty" block at the bottom, or drop them from the example entirely while the code keeps reading them.
3. **The setup output doesn't point anywhere.** `npm run setup` could finish by printing "Open http://localhost:3000 → Settings → AI access to add your key."
4. **Keys are split across two places.** AI keys are under "AI access" and bank keys under "Connected banks". If you want literally one "Keys and connections" section in Settings, I can group them. Otherwise the current split is fine; the main fix is a pointer.
5. **Small things worth checking:** the first run on Windows may show a mkcert trust prompt (the README mentions it, only under the bank section), and Docker Desktop must be running before setup. Nothing in the README says so.

## Questions before I change anything

- Should **`.env.example` drop the legacy key lines entirely**, or keep them marked as overrides? I'd keep them, moved to the bottom.
- Do you want a **single "Keys and connections" section** in Settings, or keep AI access and Connected banks separate and just fix the README and setup messages? I'd fix the docs and messages first; that's a small change.
- Should I also do a fresh-install test (new clone, new Docker project name, not your volumes) to find setup problems I can't see from reading? It won't touch your workspace.

# Moneo's self-hosted backend: Postgres plus the open-source Supabase services the app talks to
# (Auth, PostgREST, Storage), behind one gateway. Every port binds to 127.0.0.1 only, and
# `npm run setup` writes fresh secrets to .env, which Compose reads for the ${...} values.
# Image versions match Supabase CLI 3.0.0.
name: moneo

services:
  db:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.11.0.011
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "config_file=/etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf", "-c", "log_min_messages=fatal"]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_HOST: /var/run/postgresql
      POSTGRES_USER: supabase_admin
      POSTGRES_DB: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?run npm run setup}
      PGPASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?run npm run setup}
      JWT_EXP: 3600
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:${DB_PORT:-54322}:5432"]
    volumes:
      - ./docker/db/roles.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init-scripts/99-roles.sql:ro
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "postgres", "-h", "localhost"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40

  auth:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/gotrue:v2.197.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      API_EXTERNAL_URL: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1
      GOTRUE_API_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      GOTRUE_API_PORT: 9999
      GOTRUE_DB_DRIVER: postgres
      GOTRUE_DB_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://supabase_auth_admin:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/postgres
      GOTRUE_SITE_URL: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      GOTRUE_URI_ALLOW_LIST: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      GOTRUE_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
      GOTRUE_JWT_EXP: 3600
      GOTRUE_JWT_AUD: authenticated
      GOTRUE_JWT_DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME: authenticated
      GOTRUE_JWT_ADMIN_ROLES: service_role
      # The one owner account is created by setup; nobody can sign up.
      GOTRUE_DISABLE_SIGNUP: "true"
      GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_EMAIL_ENABLED: "true"
      GOTRUE_MAILER_AUTOCONFIRM: "true"
      GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_PHONE_ENABLED: "false"
      GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_ANONYMOUS_USERS_ENABLED: "false"
      GOTRUE_SECURITY_REFRESH_TOKEN_ROTATION_ENABLED: "true"
      GOTRUE_SECURITY_REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_INTERVAL: 10
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9999/health"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40

  rest:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgrest:v16.5
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      PGRST_DB_URI: postgresql://authenticator:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/postgres
      PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS: public,graphql_public
      PGRST_DB_EXTRA_SEARCH_PATH: public,extensions
      PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS: 1000
      PGRST_DB_ANON_ROLE: anon
      PGRST_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}

  storage:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/storage-api:v1.88.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://supabase_storage_admin:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/postgres
      ANON_KEY: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY}
      SERVICE_KEY: ${SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}
      AUTH_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
      STORAGE_BACKEND: file
      FILE_STORAGE_BACKEND_PATH: /var/lib/storage
      FILE_SIZE_LIMIT: 52428800
      TENANT_ID: stub
      GLOBAL_S3_BUCKET: stub
      STORAGE_S3_REGION: local
      ENABLE_IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION: "false"
    volumes: ["storage-data:/var/lib/storage"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1:5000/status"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40

  # One URL for the app's Supabase client: /auth/v1, /rest/v1 and /storage/v1.
  gateway:
    image: caddy:2.10.2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { auth: { condition: service_healthy }, rest: { condition: service_started }, storage: { condition: service_healthy } }
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:${API_PORT:-54321}:8000"]
    volumes: ["./docker/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro"]

volumes:
  db-data:
  storage-data:

if (!existsSync(ENV)) copyFileSync(".env.example", ENV);
let text = readFileSync(ENV, "utf8");
const read = key => text.match(new RegExp(`^${key}=(.*)$`, "m"))?.[1].trim().replace(/^"(.*)"$/, "$1") ?? "";

  // PostgREST caches the schema; reload it after migrations.
  if (pending.length) await db`notify pgrst, 'reload schema'`;
} finally {

}

// The owner signs in automatically (see proxy.ts); the password only lives in .env.
const response = await fetch(`${read("NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL")}/auth/v1/admin/users`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${read("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")}`, apikey: read("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"), "content-type": "application/json" },

});
const body = await response.json().catch(() => ({}));
if (!response.ok && body.error_code !== "email_exists") throw new Error(`Could not create the owner account: ${response.status} ${JSON.stringify(body)}`);
console.log(response.ok ? "Created the owner account." : "Owner account exists.");
// Enable Banking only accepts https:// return addresses, so the bank sends you back to
// https://localhost:3443. mkcert (the tool Next.js uses for local HTTPS) makes a certificate that
// only this computer trusts; the first run may ask you to allow it.
try {
  // Browsers only: skip the Java keystore, which needs admin rights and which Moneo does not use.
  process.env.TRUST_STORES = "system,nss";
  const { createSelfSignedCertificate } = createRequire(import.meta.url)("next/dist/lib/mkcert.js");
  if (!(await createSelfSignedCertificate("localhost", ".data"))) throw new Error("mkcert did not create a certificate");
  console.log("Local HTTPS certificate for bank connections is ready.");
} catch (error) {
  console.warn(`Could not create the local HTTPS certificate (${error.message}). Bank connections need it; rerun setup to try again.`);
}

console.log("\nDone. Start Moneo with: npm run build && npm start");

# Backlog

## In-app service keys: follow-ups
Keys for OpenAI, OpenRouter and Enable Banking are entered in the app (Settings → AI access, Import → Connected banks) and sealed in `service_keys`.
- Optional one-click "Move to the app" that copies a key still in `.env` into the database; today the `.env` value is used until a key is saved in the app, and nothing is removed from `.env`.
- Enable Banking's `GET /application` response may list the registered redirect URLs; warn on save when `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` is missing instead of waiting for `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- `scripts/voice-call-check.mjs` still reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment.
- Keys are cached for 5 seconds per process; a second server process sees a change within that time.

## Self-hosted: phone access from anywhere
Open Moneo on your phone from any network, like T3 Code, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).
- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.
- Bank connections from the phone: register the tunnel's `https://…/api/bank/callback` as a second redirect URL in Enable Banking, and send the bank back to whichever address the owner started from (laptop: `https://localhost:3443`).
- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.

## Multi-currency on Home
Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.
- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).
- Net worth chart: plots only display-currency balances and valuations; convert others with the rate dated on or before each month end.
- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.
- Budgets and Coming up: amounts in other currencies are left out.

# Backlog

## In-app service keys: follow-ups
Keys for OpenAI, OpenRouter and Enable Banking are entered in the app (Settings → AI access, Import → Connected banks) and sealed in `service_keys`.
- Optional one-click "Move to the app" that copies a key still in `.env` into the database; today the `.env` value is used until a key is saved in the app, and nothing is removed from `.env`.
- Enable Banking's `GET /application` response may list the registered redirect URLs; warn on save when `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` is missing instead of waiting for `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- `scripts/voice-call-check.mjs` still reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment.
- Keys are cached for 5 seconds per process; a second server process sees a change within that time.

## Self-hosted: phone access from anywhere
Open Moneo on your phone from any network, like T3 Code, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).
- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.
- Bank connections from the phone: register the tunnel's `https://…/api/bank/callback` as a second redirect URL in Enable Banking, and send the bank back to whichever address the owner started from (laptop: `https://localhost:3443`).
- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.

## Multi-currency on Home
Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.
- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).
- Net worth chart: plots only display-currency balances and valuations; convert others with the rate dated on or before each month end.
- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.
- Budgets and Coming up: amounts in other currencies are left out.

# ── Moneo configuration ──
# You don't need to edit this file. `npm run setup` copies it to .env and fills in every value.

JWT_SECRET=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=

# Authorizes the background job routes (summaries, review recovery, bank and Scalable sync).
CRON_SECRET=

# ── Development only: QA login for Playwright (written by scripts/e2e-auth.mjs) ──
E2E_USER_EMAIL=
E2E_USER_PASSWORD=

content.content:
bug documentation duplicate enhancement good first issue help wanted invalid question wontfix 
## Scalable: follow-ups

- Portfolio value chart before the first sync: rebuild past values from Scalable's trades (`list_portfolio_transactions`, all pages) and each security's price history (`get_security_chart`), including sold securities and cash flows. Today the chart starts at the first sync and fills in daily.
- Scalable's suitability/appropriateness warnings are not shown on trade cards yet; orders that need one are sent to the Scalable app. Show the warning text with an accept checkbox and pass `acknowledgementIds`.
- Not offered from chat yet: stop orders, savings plans, watchlist edits, price alerts.
- Cancelling an order is tested only against the local stand-in; check it once against a real open order.
- Per-position price charts on Wealth (a small 1-month line from `get_security_chart`) and news headlines when a position is opened.

## In-app service keys: follow-ups
Keys for OpenAI, OpenRouter and Enable Banking are entered in the app (Settings → AI access, Import → Connected banks) and sealed in `service_keys`.
- Optional one-click "Move to the app" that copies a key still in `.env` into the database; today the `.env` value is used until a key is saved in the app, and nothing is removed from `.env`.
- Enable Banking's `GET /application` response may list the registered redirect URLs; warn on save when `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` is missing instead of waiting for `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- `scripts/voice-call-check.mjs` still reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment.
- Keys are cached for 5 seconds per process; a second server process sees a change within that time.

## Self-hosted: phone access from anywhere
Open Moneo on your phone from any network, like T3 Code, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).
- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.
- Bank connections from the phone: register the tunnel's `https://…/api/bank/callback` as a second redirect URL in Enable Banking, and send the bank back to whichever address the owner started from (laptop: `https://localhost:3443`).
- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.

## Multi-currency on Home
Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.
- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).
- Net worth chart: plots only display-currency balances and valuations; convert others with the rate dated on or before each month end.
- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.
- Budgets and Coming up: amounts in other currencies are left out.

lines: -- Portfolio value chart before the first sync: rebuild past values from Scalable's trades (`list_portfolio_transactions`, all pages) and each security's price history (`get_security_chart`), including sold securities and cash flows. Today the chart starts at the first sync and fills in daily.

-- Scalable's suitability/appropriateness warnings are not shown on trade cards yet; orders that need one are sent to the Scalable app. Show the warning text with an accept checkbox and pass `acknowledgementIds`.
-- Not offered from chat yet: stop orders, savings plans, watchlist edits, price alerts.
-- Cancelling an order is tested only against the local stand-in; check it once against a real open order.
-- Per-position price charts on Wealth (a small 1-month line from `get_security_chart`) and news headlines when a position is opened.
-Keys for OpenAI, OpenRouter and Enable Banking are entered in the app (Settings → AI access, Import → Connected banks) and sealed in `service_keys`.
-- Optional one-click "Move to the app" that copies a key still in `.env` into the database; today the `.env` value is used until a key is saved in the app, and nothing is removed from `.env`.

-- Enable Banking's `GET /application` response may list the registered redirect URLs; warn on save when `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` is missing instead of waiting for `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED`.
-- Keys are cached for 5 seconds per process; a second server process sees a change within that time.

-Open Moneo on your phone from any network, like T3 Code, with nothing to install on the phone. Moneo only listens on 127.0.0.1 today, and it signs its owner in automatically, so any remote access must add a login first (an `APP_PASSWORD` sign-in, or Cloudflare Access).

-- Options weighed: Tailscale Funnel (free, fixed `*.ts.net` URL, nothing on the phone), Cloudflare Tunnel (free tunnel; a fixed URL needs your own domain, about $10/yr), or Tailscale with its phone app (private, no password needed).
-- HTTPS is required for voice: browsers only give web pages the microphone over a secure connection.

-- Bank connections from the phone: register the tunnel's `https://…/api/bank/callback` as a second redirect URL in Enable Banking, and send the bank back to whichever address the owner started from (laptop: `https://localhost:3443`).

-- Callbacks: ChatGPT sign-in only accepts a 127.0.0.1 callback and Scalable's login accepts localhost freely, so both are connected from the computer Moneo runs on; their syncs then work from anywhere.
-Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.
-- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).
-- Net worth chart: plots only display-currency balances and valuations; convert others with the rate dated on or before each month end.
-- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.
-- Budgets and Coming up: amounts in other currencies are left out.
